citations.claim: energy conserved just before impact at step 10
heavy body gains huge speed after oblique impact
total energy explodes 8.5x at first violating step 11 despite no controller work

counterfactual.change: moved body 1 start y from 9.3 to 7.0 so the fast body misses the falling body; all else identical, energy stays conserved and no violation in 11 steps

explanation: Oblique high-speed circle-circle impact injects energy: at step 10 bodies approach with speeds ~9.8 and ~56.6 and conserved energy ~3451J, but by step 11 after the glancing contact (gap 0.03) speeds are ~66.9 and ~53.3 with energy ~29442J. Inelastic (e=0) variant still violates, so it is not restitution gain; missing the collision removes it. Likely cause is incorrect impulse resolution for oblique contacts with large mass ratio at high relative velocity within substeps (e.g. normal miscomputed or positional correction adding velocity, repeated impulses per substep).
vision_note: Two small blue circles in the upper-right move slightly toward each other across steps 8 to 10 and come into close glancing contact at step 11. There is no large positional jump, wall, controller body, or waypoint visible, just the onset of contact.
